{{Current events|year=2020|month=03|day=10|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Arts and culture
*The [[Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival]] in [[Indio, California]], is postponed for the first time ever. The festival has been moved from April 2020 to October 2020 due to the [[2019–20 coronavirus pandemic|coronavirus pandemic]]. [https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/music/story/2020-03-10/coachella-rescheduled-postponed-stagecoach-october (''Los Angeles Times'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/10/arts/music/coronavirus-coachella-postponed.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Business and economy
*[[Black Monday (2020)|Black Monday]]
**After a 2,000-point drop on Monday, the [[Dow Jones Industrial Average|DJIA]] futures gain 1,100 points before the [[NYSE]] opening bell. [https://www.cnn.com/business/live-news/stock-market-news-today-031020/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Socio-economic impact of the 2019–20 coronavirus pandemic]]
**The [[President of the European Commission]] [[Ursula von der Leyen]] announces an European 25 bilion euro fund to face the coronavirus crisis. [https://www.euronews.com/2020/03/09/commission-tries-to-coordinate-response-to-covid-19-virus-across-eu (Euronews)]

;Health and environment
*[[2019–20 coronavirus pandemic]]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Italy]], [[2020 Italy coronavirus lockdown]]
***Italy enters the first day of the nationwide lockdown as the number of infected reaches 10,149. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/world-asia-51811969 (BBC)]
***[[Roberto Stella]], the president of the medical guild in [[Varese]], [[Lombardy]], has died at the age of 67 after contracting the virus. [http://www.ansa.it/lombardia/notizie/2020/03/11/coronavirus-morto-presidente-ordine-medici-varese_d988ce99-eadb-4c7a-ba9a-f925736d82a2.html (Ansa)]
***[[Riot]]s continue for the third day in Italian prisons after family visitations were suspended due to the coronavirus pandemic. Four more inmates died in the incidents, bringing the death toll to 12. The 22 inmates that escaped in [[Foggia]], [[Apulia]], are still wanted. [https://www.ilfattoquotidiano.it/2020/03/10/coronavirus-carceri-in-rivolta-altri-3-detenuti-morti-a-rieti-nuove-proteste-a-siracusa-e-caserta-a-foggia-evasione-di-massa-23-ricercati-la-procura-di-milano-apre-inchiesta-sulla-sommossa-a-san/5730183/ (Il Fatto Quotidiano)]
***[[President of the European Parliament]] [[David Sassoli]] self-isolates after visiting Italy. [https://www.politico.eu/article/european-parliaments-sassoli-to-work-from-home-as-coronavirus-precaution/ (Politico)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Japan]]
***The [[Cabinet of Japan]] passes a bill that allows [[Prime Minister of Japan|Prime Minister]] [[Shinzō Abe]] to declare a [[state of emergency]] over the coronavirus if necessary. [https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/en/news/20200310_11/ (NHK)]
**[[2019–20 coronavirus pandemic in mainland China]]
***[[Communist Party of China|Chinese Communist Party]] [[General Secretary of the Communist Party of China|general secretary]] [[Xi Jinping]] visits [[Wuhan]], the epicentre and origin of the [[2019–20 coronavirus pandemic|pandemic]], after an unprecedented [[2020 Hubei lockdowns|lockdown]] of the central city of 11 million people. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-china/xi-visits-wuhan-signaling-tide-turning-in-chinas-coronavirus-battle-idUSKBN20X01F (Reuters)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Moldova]]
***[[Moldova]] bans all foreigners from entering the country via plane who have been to any country with confirmed cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/moldova-bans-foreigners-on-all-flights-from-countries-with-coronavirus (The Straits Times)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Spain]] 
***Member of the [[Congress of Deputies]] and [[City Council of Madrid|Madrid's city councilor]] [[Javier Ortega Smith]] becomes the first of Spain's high profile infected by the coronavirus. He participated in a political event on Sunday with 9000 people. The Board of the Congress suspends this week's plenary activity after the 52 lawmakers of [[Vox (political party)|Vox]] are called to stay at home. [https://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20200310/474078641783/javier-ortega-smith-coronavirus-covid-19-vox-positivo.html (''La Vanguardia'')] [https://www.elperiodico.com/es/politica/20200310/el-congreso-suspende-su-actividad-7883144 (''El Periódico'')]
***Community of [[La Rioja (Spain)|La Rioja]] suspends all classes for two weeks. [https://www.eldiario.es/sociedad/Rioja-cierra-colegios-universidades-quince_0_1004399771.html (''el diario.es'')]
***The [[Ministry of Development (Spain)|Ministry of Transports]] announces the cancellation of all flights between Spain and Italy. [https://www.elmundo.es/ciencia-y-salud/salud/2020/03/10/5e673016fdddfff7168b45fb.html (''El Mundo'')]
***[[Argentine]] saxophonist [[Marcelo Peralta]] has died in [[Madrid]] after contracting coronavirus. [https://radiomitre.cienradios.com/el-saxofonista-argentino-marcelo-peralta-murio-por-coronavirus-en-madrid/ (Radio Mitre)]
***[[UNESCO]]'s intangible cultural heritage of humanity of [[Falles|Les Falles]] of [[Valencia]] are postponed for the fifth time in its history. [https://www.elperiodico.com/es/sociedad/20200310/coronavirus-ultimas-noticias-directo-7817968 (''El Periódico'')]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Iran]]
***[[Iran]] reports 881 new confirmed cases and 54 more COVID-19 deaths, the highest number of deaths in a single 24-hour period in the country to date, bringing the total to 8042 cases and 291 deaths. [https://www.trtworld.com/europe/iran-reports-highest-one-day-death-toll-as-italy-on-lockdown-34431 (TRT World)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in the Czech Republic]]
***The [[Czech Republic]] suspends all schools and bans all events hosting more than 100 people indefinitely in order to contain the virus, according to Prime Minister [[Andrej Babiš]]. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2020-03-10/czech-republic-closing-schools-banning-events-to-fight-coronavirus-spread (U.S. News)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Morocco]]
***The first death in [[Morocco]] is reported, an 89-year-old woman with pre-existing health conditions. [https://www.hespress.com/societe/462577.html (Hespress)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Greece]]
***[[Greece|Greek]] [[Ministry of Health (Greece)|Minister of Health]] [[Vasilis Kikilias]] announces that the country's schools and universities will remain closed for two weeks. [https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/2020/03/10/world/europe/10reuters-health-coronavirus-greece-education.html (The New York Times)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Denmark]] 
***Denmark reports a sharp increase in COVID-19 patients, with 174 new cases in the past 24 hours, totaling 264 cases in the whole country. [https://bnonews.com/index.php/2020/02/the-latest-coronavirus-cases/ (''BNO News'')] 
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Austria]]
***Head of the [[House of Habsburg-Lorraine]] and former MEP [[Karl von Habsburg|Archduke Karl von Habsburg]] tests positive for COVID-19 becoming the first member of a royal family to test positive. [https://www.salzburg24.at/news/oesterreich/kaiserenkel-karl-habsburg-positiv-auf-coronavirus-getestet-84629368 (Salzburg24)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Turkey]]
***The first COVID-19 case in [[Turkey]] is confirmed. [https://www.ntv.com.tr/turkiye/saglik-bakani-fahrettin-kocadan-corona-virus-aciklamasi-turkiyede-ilk-corona-virus-vakasi,7fRCdOc5sk2O7tbTd9z0Ug (NTV)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Poland]]
***[[Poland]]'s [[Ministry of National Defence (Poland)|Ministry of National Defence]] tweets that [[Armed Forces General Command (Poland)|General Commander]] [[Jarosław Mika]] has tested positive for COVID-19 after returning from Germany, and becomes [[NATO]]'s highest-ranking member of armed forces infected. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-poland-military/top-polish-general-has-coronavirus-defence-ministry-idUKKBN20X1YH?il=0 (''Reuters'')]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Paraguay]]
***[[Paraguay]] suspends all school and university activities and large-scale public events for 15 days as a measure of control due to the coronavirus pandemic. [https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/2020/03/10/world/americas/10reuters-health-cornavirus-paraguay.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Bolivia]]
***[[Bolivia]] confirms its two first cases. [https://www.brusselstimes.com/news-contents/world/99940/coronavirus-first-cases-in-bolivia-honduras-and-cuba/ (Brussels Time)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Vatican City]]
***[[Saint Peter's Square]] and [[St. Peter's Basilica]] closes to tourists between 10 March and 3 April after Italy lockdown [https://www.theguardian.com/world/video/2020/mar/10/st-peters-square-before-and-after-italys-nationwide-lockdown-video (The Guardian)]
**[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in the United States]]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Colorado]]
****[[Colorado]] Governor [[Jared Polis]] declares a state of emergency after a total of 17 presumptive cases of COVID-19 are reported in the state. [https://krdo.com/news/2020/03/10/gov-jared-polis-gives-briefing-on-covid-19-with-state-health-officials/ (KRDO)]
***[[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Connecticut]]
****[[Connecticut]] Governor [[Ned Lamont]] declares a civil preparedness and public health emergency in response to the coronavirus. [https://www.wtnh.com/news/health/coronavirus/gov-lamont-to-declare-civil-preparedness-public-health-emergencies-in-response-to-coronavirus/ (WTNH)]

;Law and crime
*The [[Canadian government]] presents a bill that would impose a nationwide ban on [[conversion therapy]] that would include minors. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-51773586 (BBC)]
;Politics and elections
*[[2020 amendments to the Constitution of Russia]]
**[[Vladimir Putin]] backs a constitutional amendment that would allow him to remain in power after 2024 and make a  [[president for life|lifetime presidency]] possible.  [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/putin-backs-amendment-allowing-him-remain-power-n1154101 (NBC News)]
*[[2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries]]
**Voters in six U.S. states cast their ballots in the primary elections. Former [[Vice President of the United States|Vice President]] [[Joe Biden]] wins the [[2020 Mississippi Democratic primary|Mississippi]], [[2020 Missouri Democratic primary|Missouri]], [[2020 Michigan Democratic primary|Michigan]], and [[2020 Idaho Democratic primary|Idaho]] primaries and is ahead in [[2020 Washington Democratic primary|Washington]] (which has not finished tallying votes),  while [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Bernie Sanders]] wins [[2020 North Dakota Democratic primary|North Dakota]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2020/03/10/us/elections/results-primary-elections-michigan-washington.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.cnn.com/2020/03/11/politics/2020-primary-election-takeaways/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Venezuelan protests (2014–present)]]
**Riot police repels [[Venezuela]]'s opposition march downtown [[Caracas]] that aimed to regain control of [[National Assembly (Venezuela)|the national legislature]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/latino/venezuela-opposition-marches-congress-showdown-maduro-n1153921 (NBC News)]
